samples.summary: The new "every tab-scoped v1 write verb" enumeration omits the three new tab verbs (DELETE tab, reorder, duplicate), and tabs.controller.spec never tries a hostile tabId either
samples.evidence: worksheet-lookup.util.spec.ts:117 declares "Every tab-scoped v1 write verb, not just the images one" and then enumerates 20 verbs from worksheet/rules/styles/charts/images/dimensions/filterPivot/cells/structure — but `ApiV1TabsController.remove`, `.move` (reorder) and `.duplicate` are absent (grep for `tabs|Tabs` in that spec returns no matches). Those three are new in this diff, take `:tabId` straight off the URL, and `remove`/`move` resolve it through `resolveDelete`/`resolveMove` in tab-ops.ts:78 / :121, which are plain truthiness checks (`const tab = root.tabs?.[tabId]; if (!tab) return not_found`) — exactly the pattern the whole `worksheet-lookup.util.ts` docblock says is insufficient because a live Yorkie object proxy answers `toJSON`/`getID`/`toJS` with a truthy function. tabs.controller.spec.ts only tests `'nope'` ('404s an unknown tab' at the delete/move/duplicate describes), never `__proto__`/`toJSON`/`getID`. So `DELETE .../tabs/toJSON` and `POST .../tabs/toJSON/reorder` have no test at all, and the destructive `applyDelete` (`delete root.tabs[tabId]`, `root.tabOrder.splice`) would run on a non-tab key with nothing to catch it.
searchedFor: read tabs.controller.spec.ts delete/move/duplicate describes in the diff

samples.summary: The resolve response's `resolvedAt` is never asserted to be a plain number / JSON-serializable, though the diff explicitly guards the analogous reply bug
samples.evidence: The spec goes out of its way for the reply path — "`buildReply` stores `createdAt` as a Long (a JS `bigint`), which `res.json()` refuses outright… Assert the whole payload survives serialisation" with `expect(typeof reply.comment.createdAt).toBe('number')` and `expect(() => JSON.stringify(reply)).not.toThrow()`. The `setResolved` tests assert only `resolved.resolved`, `resolved.resolvedBy` and `reopened.resolvedAt` being `undefined`; nothing asserts `typeof resolved.resolvedAt === 'number'` or that the resolve response stringifies. `applySetResolved` writes a Long (`toYorkieMs`) and only `copyThread` converts it back — a regression there would 500 every PATCH resolve with no failing test.

samples.summary: "Editing does not notify" is stated as behavior but no test asserts createFromComment is not called on edit or delete
samples.evidence: comments.controller.ts's `editComment` carries the comment "// Editing does not notify: the recipients were told when the comment was written…". The `ApiV1CommentsController notifications` describe covers thread/reply/resolve/reopen and the actor-exclusion case, but there is no `expect(notificationService.createFromComment).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` after an `editComment`, `deleteComment` or `deleteThread`. If a future change wires notify into edit, duplicate inbox rows would ship green.

samples.summary: 'keeps a concurrent edit to another slide' cannot fail for the regression it names — a whole-array replacement would pass it too
samples.evidence: The test comments claim "The whole reason these verbs exist beside `PUT .../content`: only the one slide is written, so nothing else in the array is replaced", then asserts `expect(slides()[0]).toBe(untouched)` and `expect(slides()[0].elements[0]).toEqual(peerEdit)`. A last-write-wins implementation of `root.slides = [...slides, newSlide]` preserves the identity of the existing slide objects, so both assertions still hold; the test does not distinguish granular splice from array reassignment. (slide-ops.spec.ts's 'carries only the new slide, never a replacement deck' does assert `change.kind === 'insert'`, so the behavior is covered elsewhere — this controller test is the one that overstates what it proves.)

samples.summary: The non-slides document gate is tested only for `add`; layouts/duplicate/move/remove have no type-gate test
samples.evidence: `assertSlidesDocument` runs on all five handlers, but only `it('refuses a non-slides document before opening Yorkie')` exercises it, and only through `controller.add`. A handler that forgot the `await this.assertSlidesDocument(...)` call (e.g. `remove`, which is destructive) would let a caller delete slides out of a sheet/doc-typed Yorkie root with the suite green.

samples.summary: The route-collision detector has no negative case proving it detects a collision, and its companion assertion is a magic-number tripwire
samples.evidence: `it('has no two handlers on the same method and path')` asserts `expect(collisions).toEqual([])` against the live module. If the metadata reads silently return nothing (wrong `PATH_METADATA` key, prototype walk missing decorated methods, `controllers` metadata key change), `collisions` is `[]` and the test passes while detecting nothing — the whole guard is vacuous. There is no fixture controller pair proving a known collision is reported. The sibling `expect(controllers.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(18)` is a partial guard against the empty-list case but is a hand-maintained constant, not a proof the extraction works.
searchedFor: searched for any fixture/negative-case describe in the same file

samples.summary: `sheets images set` stdin path is never tested — only `--data`
samples.evidence: The handler has two input paths: `--data` and an async stdin drain (`for await (const chunk of process.stdin)`). packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts's 'sheets images' describe only ever passes `--data` ('accepts the envelope its own get prints' and 'rejects a payload that is neither an array nor that envelope'). The stdin branch — including its distinct error message wording ('on stdin' vs 'in --data') — has no coverage, and `sheets images get | sheets images set` is the documented workflow.

samples.summary: duplicateTab's non-sheet metadata carry-over (kind/datasourceId/query) and applyDelete on a worksheet-less tab are untested
samples.evidence: `duplicateTab` (tab-ops.ts) selectively copies `source.kind` (dropping only `'pivot'`), `source.datasourceId` and `source.query`; the new tab-ops.spec tests only name-uniquing, comments-drop, chart repointing and pivot-drop. Nothing asserts a `datasource` tab's `datasourceId`/`query` survive or that a non-pivot `kind` is carried. Likewise `applyDelete`'s documented guard "The worksheet is deleted only when it exists — a `datasource`/`lakehouse` tab has metadata and no `sheets` entry" has no test deleting such a tab.
searchedFor: tab-ops.spec.ts 'resolveDelete / applyDelete' and 'duplicateTab' describes in the diff

samples.summary: parsePdfAnchor's missing/non-object `rect` and non-numeric rect fields are untested, as is `asObject`'s non-object-body rejection
samples.evidence: comments.controller.spec.ts's PDF describe covers only an out-of-range `w: 2` and `pageIndex: -1`. `rect` absent, `rect` an array, and `rect.x` a string each have their own BadRequestException branch in `parsePdfAnchor`, and `asObject(body, 'body')` rejecting an array/non-object body has no test on any of the six handlers.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. worksheet-lookup.util.spec.ts:118-304 declares it covers "Every tab-scoped v1 write verb" and enumerates 20 verbs, but never imports or invokes ApiV1TabsController — remove/move(reorder)/duplicate are absent. tabs.controller.spec.ts exercises those three verbs only with the benign id 'nope' (:218, :286, :353); its two toJSON tests (:309, :334) proxy the *source worksheet* while still addressing the real 'tab-1', so they test unwrapJson, not hostile-key resolution. tab-ops.spec.ts likewise uses only 'tab-nope' for resolveDelete/resolveMove not_found (:112-119, :159-165). I searched repo-wide for __proto__ across packages/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,mjs}, for 'toJSON' literals, all packages/backend/src/api/**/*.spec.ts, every TabsController reference (only sheet-document.util.spec.ts document-type checks and api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts guard-metadata checks), and the whole packages/backend/test e2e dir (no tabs routes) — no counterexample. The gap is over live destructive code: tabs.controller.ts:172 routes DELETE through resolveDelete's truthiness check (tab-ops.ts:78-79) into applyDelete's `delete root.tabs[tabId]` / `tabOrder.splice` (tab-ops.ts:102-107), while the sibling duplicate handler explicitly guards the same hazard with safeWorksheetRecordKeys (tabs.controller.ts:259) — an asymmetry nothing in the test suite pins. Untested guard weakening on a destructive write path meets the major bar.
